data.one_liner: Programmatically restart your Flutter application with callbacks, animations, and advanced control.
data.what_it_does: AppRestarter allows you to restart a Flutter application programmatically by wrapping the root widget and calling a static restart function. It supports custom transition animations, delays, conditional logic, and lifecycle callbacks for cleanup and re-initialization.
use_when: You need to completely reset the application state and widget tree, such as on user logout or language change.
You want custom transition animations or a delay when restarting the app.
You need to run asynchronous initialization or cleanup logic before or after a restart.
avoid_when: You only need to rebuild a single screen or local widget subtree.
You prefer terminating the native OS process instead of resetting the Flutter widget tree.
strengths: Zero dependencies and pure Flutter implementation.
Supports custom animations, delayed restarts, and conditional execution.
Includes async lifecycle callbacks for state cleanup and service re-initialization (e.g. GetX).
weaknesses: Does not terminate the underlying OS process; it only forces a rebuild from the root widget using KeyedSubtree.
Requires manual re-initialization of global dependencies (like GetX services) after a restart.
data.setup_notes: Wrap your root widget (above MaterialApp or CupertinoApp) with the AppRestarter widget.
